commits.edited_message:
lib|tests: Handle OOM when copying encodingName in XML_ParserReset

When XML_ParserReset(parser, encodingName) is called with a non-NULL
encodingName, parserInit() invokes copyString() to allocate and store
the protocol encoding name. If memory allocation fails, copyString()
returns NULL.

Unlike parserCreate() and XML_SetEncoding(), which both check
(encodingName && ! parser->m_protocolEncodingName) and fail cleanly,
XML_ParserReset() previously ignored this allocation failure and returned
XML_TRUE. This silently dropped the requested encoding, leaving
m_protocolEncodingName as NULL while reporting success to the caller.

Verify up front that the encoding name can be stored, before any parser
state is torn down, so that a failed reset leaves the parser unchanged.
Keep reporting the failure after parserInit() as well: set
parser->m_errorCode to XML_ERROR_NO_MEMORY and return XML_FALSE.
Also add a unit test test_alloc_reset_encoding in alloc_tests.c.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

lib: Call unknown encoding release before teardown

The application-defined release callback may access the parser, e.g. to
query the current position, so it has to run while the parse buffer and
position state are still intact.  Move the call ahead of the teardown
in both XML_ParserReset() and XML_ParserFree().

callUnknownEncodingRelease() no longer clears m_unknownEncodingRelease
and m_unknownEncodingData afterwards: XML_ParserReset() reinitializes
both via parserInit(), and XML_ParserFree() destroys the parser right
after.

Signed-off-by: Junki Lee <junkilee80@gmail.com>

Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

coupling:
The defect is a double-invocation of the application-defined unknown-encoding release callback, spread across the two commits that both touch XML_ParserReset()/teardown.

Commit 8d96d7e moves the release callback ahead of the teardown in XML_ParserReset() and XML_ParserFree() and, as part of that refactor, stops callUnknownEncodingRelease() from clearing m_unknownEncodingRelease/m_unknownEncodingData after invoking the callback. In isolation this is unobservable and correct: on the reset path parserInit() (always reached) reinitializes both fields, and on the free path the parser is destroyed immediately after, so no code can ever re-read the stale fields.

Commit 5796b80 adds handling for OOM when copying the encoding name in XML_ParserReset(). The edited version performs a pre-flight copyString() and returns XML_FALSE early - placed, for its 'leave the parser unchanged on failure' goal, after the release callback but before any teardown, so crucially before parserInit() runs. In isolation this is also correct: with the original wrapper still NULLing the release fields, a failed reset leaves m_unknownEncodingRelease == NULL and XML_ParserFree() skips the callback.

Only the composition is faulty: the release callback runs at the top of XML_ParserReset() (8d96d7e's ordering), the fields are no longer cleared by the wrapper (8d96d7e's edit), the pre-flight allocation fails and XML_ParserReset() returns before parserInit() can reinitialize them (5796b80's early return), so XML_ParserFree() invokes the same release callback a second time for the same cookie. The release callback exists precisely so the application can free its cookie there, so a conforming application double-frees (ASan: attempting double-free, SIGABRT).

A correct fix must reason across both commits: keeping the field clearing in callUnknownEncodingRelease() (undoing 8d96d7e's wrapper change) makes the pointer NULL when XML_ParserFree() checks it, and removing or relocating 5796b80's early return (e.g. checking only after parserInit(), as the original commit did) guarantees parserInit() clears the fields on every reset failure path. Fixing either single commit's diff alone removes the bug; neither diff is wrong on its own.

pocs.entry_point: XML_ParserReset/XML_ParserFree (libexpat public C API, parser created with XML_ParserCreate_MM and a failing allocation)
